statement.text:
(a) Let $S$ be an infinite-type surface and $\varphi$ a mapping class for which there is
a (marked) conformal structure $\Sigma$ on $S$ with respect to which $\varphi$ is realized
as a quasi-conformal homeomorphism.
Then for each quasi-conformal
structure in the connected component of Teichmüller space containing $\Sigma$,
there is a quasiconformal homeomorphism representing $\varphi$ which minimizes
the dilatation. If the infimum of the minimal dilatations for each structure
in this component is achieved and is greater than 1, is the minimizing
quasiconformal homeomorphism unique? What is the structure of such a
minimizer?
(b) If $\varphi$ is parabolic (see Remark (1) below) for $T$, must a sequence of con-
formal structures with dilatation converging to the infimum degenerate by
pinching along some sequence of essential simple closed curves? Is this
system unique? Can it depend on the component $T$?
(c) If $\varphi$ fixes more than one component $T, T'$ of $\operatorname{Teich}(S)$, can the type be dif-
ferent for $T$ and $T'$? In particular, can $\varphi$ be parabolic for $T$ and hyperbolic
for $T'$?
